question.worked_solution:
Notice that the leading coefficient is negative. To reduce the expression to a more familiar form, we can factor out $-1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-16{k}^{2}+\frac{8}{3}k-\frac{1}{9} & = \\ -(16{k}^{2}-\frac{8}{3}k+\frac{1}{9})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the quadratic expression inside the parentheses using the square of a difference  formula: 

$$
\begin{aligned}16{k}^{2}-\frac{8}{3}k+\frac{1}{9} & = \\ (4k)^{2}-\frac{8}{3}k+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2} & = \\ (4k)^{2}-2\cdot (4k\cdot \frac{1}{3})+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2} & = \\ {(4k-\frac{1}{3})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-(16{k}^{2}-\frac{8}{3}k+\frac{1}{9}) & = \\ -{(4k-\frac{1}{3})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$
